plan: My private value is $23. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This prevents overpaying if I win, and ensures I win when the item is truly worth more to me than others. Since the values are randomly drawn and independent, I can't predict others' values. By bidding $23, I maximize my potential profit - I'll win if others value the item less, and pay only the second-highest bid.

My private value is $18. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding close to $18. Since the values are randomly drawn, I have no prior history to inform a different strategy. By bidding my true value, I maximize my potential profit - if I win at a price below $18, I gain money, and if I lose, I pay nothing. I'll bid slightly under my value to give a small buffer.

My private value is $25, which means I want to maximize my potential profit. Since this is a single round with no prior history, I'll use a strategic bid slightly below my true value. Bidding exactly at $25 risks paying close to my entire value. I'll bid $22, which gives me some potential profit margin if I win. This allows me to potentially win at a price below my value while not overbidding and risking paying more than the item is worth to me.
